body: I tried to reproduce this in v4.5.rc2.official [2dd26a027] and I think I know what is happening. If I create the resource in my project's folder "res://OneIntPath.tres" and double click the resource I see it hase a "value=0" despite it not existing if I open the resource in a text editor: I thought it might be an optimization where a missing value (that exists on the class) is assumed to be 0. I added a "test" var initialized to 3 and it was missing too but assumed to be 3: I believe that any value that is the same as the default is being omitted as if I change test to anything else before saving results in the value appearing: Class ``` class_name OneIntResource extends Resource @export var value: int = 0 @export var test: int = 3 ``` Change before save ``` var t = OneIntResource.new(0) t.test = 12 ResourceSaver.save( t, # Works with any value other than 0 file_path ) ``` File in text editor ``` [gd_resource type="Resource" script_class="OneIntResource" load_steps=2 format=3] [ext_resource type="Script" path="res://TestResource.gd" id="1_64h27"] [resource] script = ExtResource("1_64h27") test = 12 ```

Ah good find, I've confirmed as well. I guess the issue is the default is assumed to be 0 even if I have an argument default in the _init override.
```
class_name OneIntResource extends Resource

@export var value: int

func _init(val: int = 3) -> void:
	value = val
```
In the above example, the resource will never be saved with value = 0, but will always be loaded as value = 3

This is an optimization, default values are not saved since
- https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/107049

@OzelotVanilla @RandomShaper @akien-mga 
I see y'all are the original authors and reviewers, what are your thoughts?
I think this optimization might cause a lot of confusion, especially with the example:
```
class_name OneIntResource extends Resource

@export var value: int

func _init(val: int = 3) -> void:
	value = val
```
Which would make saving the resource with 0 impossible.
This is the convention I've been using in my project since I can get an initialized resources with correct default values using:
`var default_resource: OneIntResource = OneIntResource.new()`
while also being able to pass any arguments in to set any fields if needed:
`var set_resource: OneIntResource = OneIntResource.new(5)`

```
@export var value: int
```
The value is 0 by default although it is not saved, no?

The value is 0 by default, but it will not be saved because of the optimization.
```
[gd_resource type="Resource" script_class="OneIntResource" load_steps=2 format=3]

[ext_resource type="Script" path="res://TestResource.gd" id="1_sb6kc"]

[resource]
script = ExtResource("1_sb6kc")
```
If this resource is loaded, our _init override will be used. 
```
func _init(val: int = 3) -> void:
	value = val
```
Since the resource file does not provide a value field, the default parameter will be used. This results in the resource being loaded as OneIntResource.new(3) essentially. That's what I'm guessing is happening?

Just double checked with this modified script for the minimal reproduction project.
```
const file_path: String = "user://OneIntPath.tres"
# Called when the node enters the scene tree for the first time.
func _ready():
	ResourceSaver.save(
		OneIntResource.new(0), # Works with any value other than 0
		file_path
	)
	var result = ResourceLoader.load(file_path)
	print(result.value)

```
It will always print 3

You can make `value` default to 3. That should make it work as expected. 

This might be a relatively edge case, you are setting value to 3 by default in `_init` but the default value of the property is 0.

(Notice: I am still a beginner for Godot Engine, and for that PR, I just commit a code suggested by another project member. So, I am not sure what I have found is guaranteed to be correct. I would be happy if you point out my mistake)

I would like to point out a behaviour when I was doing my project. GDScript seems to use the values stored in `.tres` file as a value-for-overwrite. The building of an instance may go through a process like: 

1. Build an empty object with member variable assigned by default value (a *zero* value such as `0` for `int` or `""` for `String`, or the user-specified value like `@export var test: int = 3` mentioned above)
2. Use the value stored in `.tres` file to *overwrite*. Example: `test = 4` will make that variable set as `4`.

I discovered this behaviour while I realised `_init` arguments is **not** the key-value entries stored in `.tres` file, as a result no wonder `_init` is **not** responsible for initialising when deserialising from `.tres` file 😢.

Providing this as an example (from https://github.com/OzelotVanilla/AdaptiveMusicUsingGraph/commit/78bfc816bacefa189ddf798ff67ce18973bc1fca):

For [these lines](https://github.com/OzelotVanilla/AdaptiveMusicUsingGraph/blob/4e89f37f3af7509fb23a173554e0872a726f65c0/addons/adaptive_music_using_graph__plugin/core/data_type/MusicGraph.gd#L8-L12):

```gdscript
## Array saving reference to node, sorted by node's id, from small to big.
@export var node_array: Array[MusicNode] = []:
    get = getAllNodes,
    set = loadFromNodeArray # This line was added to solve the not-loading issue
var node_dict: Dictionary[int, MusicNode] = {}
```

Even I had an `_init` like this, without the `set` line above, it will not load:
```gdscript
func _init(
    node_array: Array[MusicNode] = [],
    edge_array: Array[MusicEdge] = [],
    starting_node_id: int = -1
) -> void:
    pass
```

As the people who create that PR, I would like to agree with the behaviour of omitting default values of member variable, since it would make the `.tres` file smaller. I may suggest that add something like `@export_no_omit` to force create a key-value pair in `.tres` file.

However, I think there could be documentation to explain that loading of `.tres` is **not** calling `_init`, but overwriting values as I mentioned before.

PS: For `_init`, I found many built-in class tend to leave it zero-arg. I remembered I used a built-in function before, which can init an instance by providing class or script path as argument. But I could not pass `_init` argument of that class (it would be called like `class_got.new()` inside that built-in function). Therefore, I would like to suggest that GDScript has a convention that leave `_init` zero-arg, and assign values after initialisation.

I am confused by this part: > However, I think there could be documentation to explain that loading of .tres is not calling _init, but overwriting values as I mentioned before. From my experience, loading of `.tres` is calling `_init`. If I make the _init log being called: ``` func _init(val: int = 3) -> void: print("_init called %s" % [str(val)]) value = val ``` Then my tests show that _init is called for loading `.tres` ``` func _ready(): ResourceSaver.save( OneIntResource.new(0), # Prints 0 file_path ) var result = ResourceLoader.load(file_path) # Prints 3 ``` This can also be reproduced with debug break points. I assume Godot is not calling _init with the values from the `.tres` but I assume Godot uses a zero-arg _init as a starting point, which is where my bug comes from. My zero-arg _init still has a default value (3), but the actual value (0) is not present in the `.tres` since it was omitted for being the default value.

I think conceptually the issue I have with this optimization is:
- The default value optimization does not respect default values defined in _init
- There is no way to know that default values will be optimized out
- The optimization assumes a default value, even if one is not set, as in:
`@export var value: int`
vs
`@export var value: int = 0`

But I also recognize the issues with my approach of overloading _init with additional arguments since it messes with a lot of assumptions with the loading process.
Overall though, I do think Godot will be more resilient if resource parameters ares always saved and used during load, instead of assuming that omitting is equivalent to having the field set to it's default value.

`_init` is always called, then the saved properties are set.

Default values are not saved so the setters are not called, so the value is 3.

In this case, I am confused why `ResourceLoader.load` called the parameterized constructor instead of the parameterless constructor.

I've replaced overloading the _init function with a static initialize getter and that addresses all my concerns. Thanks for all the help and explaining!

Only when the default value of properties are different from the `_init` default arguments will cause problems, You can still use `_init` but make sure the default arguments are consistent with default values, right?
I don't think it should be reverted without considering the severity of the issue and other solutions.

You can, but then you'd have to define and maintain the default values in two separate places which seems not ideal to me. 
There would be a requirement that the default value of the property and the `_init` arguments has to be the same, which I don't think will be very obvious.

Ideally, `ResourceLoader.load` should still set the value of any fields not in the `.tres` file with the default value of the field, and not assume `_init` has done that already. But I don't know if something like that would be easy to do. This way we can avoid this issue coming up while having the optimized `.tres` files.

I've just upgraded to 4.5, and this optimization has resulted in unexpected behavior for me. For better or worse, my game currently relies on different default values in the `@export` and in the `_init`. Making them consistent will solve this issue, but I will have to carefully update my resources (I have a few hundred with this issue) to make sure I do not miss a value.

At the very least, this optimization should be mentioned in the migration guide, as it results in a breaking change for any mismatched var/_init defaults.

I think we do have some issue here.

Resource loading works as follows:
1. Instantiate the type via `ClassDB::instantiate()`. That will invoke (both in GDScript and C#) inline initializers and the constructor.
2. Apply all the property values that have been explicitly saved (because they diverge from the default).

Resource saving should therefore work with the concept of a default property value being the one it has just after the constructor has run.

Reverting the optimization would hide the problem, to some extent at least. However, I think the issue may be viewed from a different angle:

_De facto_, both GDScript and C# have a notion of the default value of a property being that in the inline initializer expression.¹² That being the case, we would have multiple possibilities towards consistency:
- a) Change the resource loader so the defaul values are applied during the instantiation of the class, after the inline initializers have run and before the constructor runs. This would imply pesky changes to `ClassDB` and the scripting modules.
- b) Change the scripting modules so the default values they provide are actually the ones just after the constructor has been run. Again, inconvenient to say the least, as parsing the scripts would require somehow running the constructors.
- c) Don't base the obtaining of default values on parse-time metadata, even remove such functionality from the scripting modules, and always rely on the values of a default-constructed instance.

Right now, I see _c)_ as the clear winner, an approach that would make everything consistent.

¹: I'm guessing GDExtension works differently, which would make this topic even trickier. (@dsnopek, can you confirm?)
²: The default property values provided by the scripting modules only include the exported properties, which may not be an issue, but it's worth pointing out.

> I'm guessing GDExtension works differently, which would make this topic even trickier. (@dsnopek, can you confirm?)

The property defaults for a class defined through GDExtension are the property values after initializing the class with its default constructor (so, the one taking no arguments). While GDExtension classes can have other constructors, we don't currently allow exposing the non-default ones to Godot, so I don't think we can have exactly this same problem?

A related (but different) issue that has come up on the GDExtension side, is that within Godot itself, you can override default property values via `ADD_PROPERTY_DEFAULT()`, but that isn't currently exposed to GDExtension - see https://github.com/godotengine/godot-cpp/issues/1706

Hopefully some of that info is helpful in this context :-)
